tasks.title: Closing-review round 3: one answerer per blocked reason, the operator before round 3, composed follow-up briefs, runnable compose examples
tasks.summary: Factory-level. wave.md step 9 maps every blocked gate reason, and each `coverage-evidence` case, to exactly one answerer with no catch-all, the uiux reasons a bounce to the uiux pass and `grader-invalid` the grader's turn; a block no builder answers is never bounced, and from its second failed round waits for the operator's logged answer, the env-failure block included; queue-and-gate.md matches row for row; `bs brief compose` composes a follow-up's brief from its `task-added` record, its own findings as scope with block markers neutralised, preflight line and gate checks included, and waivers.md routes every follow-up through it; the compose commands the docs lead with carry the worker flags and a test runs them.
tasks.objective: Factory-level fix for the three findings of the closing spec review, round 3, on plan v6 (bs-gate-bounce-run-2026-10-29#282, judge report #283, integration head f85c1b1c): f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-38ddc74d (S3), f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-5c096bd9 (S3) and f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-7d2c72ec (S4), as revised by the pre-code review of the v7 draft, round 1 (dispatch #292): f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-9c1bb4d6 (S2), f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-b3e3083c (S3), f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-29686266 (S3) and f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-2d92075f (S4), and round 2 (dispatch #298): f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-105d3733 (S3), f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-446ee7cf (S3) and f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-05cec9f9 (S4). Line numbers are at that head; the symbol named beside each is the reference if a line has moved. Task-7's design (the five branches of wave.md step 7, the `input` labels, the precedence and the tie-break) and task-8's design (`grader-invalid` in branch 2 answered by the grader's turn, the tester for the screenshots reasons, the composed preflight line and gate checks, the lint, the tester's own result file, one branch-4 return per task) stay; this task changes only what is named here, and says so where it narrows task-8's wording. (a) Findings f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-38ddc74d, f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-2d92075f and f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-b3e3083c: one answerer per blocked reason. wave.md step 9 (wave.md:484-494) names a builder for `schema-invalid`, `artifacts-missing` and the two screenshots reasons, then ends with 'the coder for every other reason' (wave.md:489), which sends `deps-missing` (step 7 branch 1), `judges-outstanding`, `uiux-spec-missing` and `uiux-visual-missing` (branch 2) to a coder. The `grader-invalid` sentence (wave.md:489-492) names the grader's turn and the epic session for one reason, as do step 7 branch 2 (wave.md:311-316), queue-and-gate.md section 5 branch 2 (queue-and-gate.md:545-550) and its table row (queue-and-gate.md:466). The rule 'A blocked task blocks itself' (wave.md:128) bounces every block to the builder. queue-and-gate.md's outcome table (queue-and-gate.md:455-472) has no `uiux-spec-missing` or `uiux-visual-missing` row and names no answerer for `artifacts-missing` or `coverage-evidence`. wave.md step 7's coverage bullet (wave.md:410-416) and that table row say a `coverage-evidence` block is fixed in the reporter or the include glob, 'not the code'. What the code does at f85c1b1c: the gate blocks on fourteen reasons, the `reason` union of gate.ts `GateOutcome`'s blocked variant (gate.ts:245-260). A `coverage-evidence` block (gate.ts:1286-1330, `gatherCoverageEvidence` gate.ts:933, coverage.ts `collectCoverageEvidence`) carries `coverageEvidence`, from which three cases read apart: `present` false (no summary after the coverage check: the reporter list, project configuration); `present` true with an `unmeasured` subject (a claimed file with no row while files beside it have one: either no test loads it or the coverage config skips it, and the gate cannot tell which); and `present` true with no `unmeasured` subject (the gate read no claims for the task id, so it marked the evidence incomplete, gate.ts:955-967). End state: step 9 lists every reason with exactly one answerer and no catch-all, `coverage-evidence` with one answerer per case of that evidence, the coder for the case the gate cannot split, as before task-9; `grader-invalid` is a judge turn's like the other three branch-2 reasons, its capped case a pointer to the grader cap's re-scope in every place that states it; queue-and-gate.md's table matches row for row; and a test keyed to the gate's own type fails when a reason has no answerer or any bullet or row names a second one. The uiux pass is a builder: escalation.ts `BUILDER_ROLES` (escalation.ts:47) is coder, tester and uiux, and wave.md step 7 (wave.md:362-368) says a re-run uiux pass is a builder dispatch the ladder governs; a probe of the built `bs escalation check` reads a uiux dispatch on a strictly higher tier after a second failed round `ok` and one on the same tier `violation`, while a reviewer re-dispatch there reads `unverifiable` (it is no builder dispatch). So `uiux-spec-missing`, `uiux-visual-missing` and a `judges-outstanding` whose `outstandingJudges` names a uiux turn are a bounce to the uiux pass (f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-105d3733), under the ladder's usual rungs, and only the grader's and the other non-builder judges' turns are judge turns. (b) Findings f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-38ddc74d and f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-29686266: the ladder for a block no builder answers. escalation.ts `readFailedRounds` (escalation.ts:169) counts every blocked `gate-outcome`, and a probe of the built `bs escalation check` at f85c1b1c shows rung 2 (`checkModelTierRung`, escalation.ts:266) after a second failed round reading `not-applicable` while nothing more runs on the task, `unverifiable` for a re-gate with no builder dispatch even after an operator's `user_prompt`, `violation` for a same-tier builder dispatch and `ok` only for a strictly higher-tier one; rung 3 (`checkOperatorRung`) wants an operator answer before any work after the third. So on one task id the only ladder-clean way past a second failed round is a higher-tier builder dispatch, and the env-failure bullet (wave.md:506-521, queue-and-gate.md:617-623) buys exactly that for a fault that is not the builder's. End state, one rule for every block no builder answers, the env-classified one included: a bare re-gate after the first failed round; from the second the task stops on its id until the operator's logged answer picks a re-scope under a new id, one strictly higher-tier builder dispatch whose causal parent is that answer, or a waiver or closure; from the third the operator rung as today. escalation.ts and budgets.yml do not change; the operator-first bound at round 2 is a playbook rule the log evidences by structure (the dispatch's `causal_parent`) and no verb enforces, an accepted gap stated beside branch 4's. The env-failure bullet (wave.md:506-521) and queue-and-gate.md's env-failure paragraph state the round-2 order once each, in the same words: the operator's answer first and only then any higher-tier builder dispatch (f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-446ee7cf). (c) Findings f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-5c096bd9 and f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-9c1bb4d6: composed follow-up briefs. A follow-up (`<epic>/followup-<fp8>`, minted by `bs findings raise` routing, attribution.ts, and recorded only as a `task-added` event, taskEvents.ts `emitFollowUpTask`) is in no plan, so briefCompose.ts `specFor` (briefCompose.ts:126-150) refuses it as `brief.task-not-in-plan`, and waivers.md step 4 (waivers.md:66-84) has the epic session hand-build its brief, a list that leaves out the preflight line and the gate checks. Everything the brief needs is in the log or the flags: its claims and epic from its `task-added` record (taskEvents.ts `readAddedTasks`, the register `bs wave next` folds follow-ups from, cli.ts:1690-1712); the five worker values from flags; the tester's `--plan` from the plan compose read (cli.ts `uiAffectingFromFlags` reads a task the plan lacks as no answer, not a refusal). The follow-up's scope is the finding routing re-minted under its id, which findingContext.ts `findingsForDispatch` leaves out of the context block on purpose (findingContext.ts:134); `bs findings list --task <followup>` (findings.ts `listFindings`) is the read that returns it. End state: compose composes a follow-up's brief from its `task-added` record, with a `scope` section holding the follow-up's own open findings read through `listFindings` for its id, beside the unchanged context block, each scope line passed through findingContext.ts `flatten`, which neutralises `<!--` and `-->` for the sibling findings block and is exported for it, not copied (f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-05cec9f9), and the preflight line and gate checks as for a plan task; waivers.md step 4 routes every follow-up through it and leaves only the acceptance criteria and the budget to the epic session. findingContext.ts changes only by exporting `flatten`; dispatchLint.ts and cli.ts do not change. (d) Finding f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-7d2c72ec: the compose lines the docs lead with omit the worker flags: dispatch.md 'Carry into the prompt' (dispatch.md:21-22), wave.md step 8 (wave.md:460-461) and worktrees-and-judges.md section 3d's coder example (worktrees-and-judges.md:379-382), which as printed exits 1 with `brief.preflight-values-required`. End state: each carries them, and a test runs every documented compose command or, for a `<role>` line, checks it names every flag compose's own refusal lists. (e) CHANGELOG.md `## Unreleased` gains an entry for `task-9-close-review-r3-fixes`. (f) The diff cap is sized from the claims, and an overrun is recorded, not blocking.
acceptance_criteria: Findings f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-38ddc74d, f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-2d92075f, f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-b3e3083c and f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-105d3733, step 9 as an exhaustive map. wave.md step 9 keeps its opening line ('Gate outcome `blocked` → bounce to the builder whose output its reason names, on the **same branch**'), followed at once by a sentence that only the reasons and cases the list below gives to a builder are bounced; keeps its tester clause (the tester re-shoots at the gate's HEAD, step 5 records the new set, and step 5's uiux visual pass reviews it) and its ladder sentence, and adds after the ladder sentence that the uiux pass is a builder too (escalation.ts `BUILDER_ROLES`), so a bounce to it is a builder dispatch the ladder counts and from the second failed round runs on a strictly higher model tier than the failing round's builder dispatch; and replaces 'the coder for every other reason' with a list of exactly one bullet per member of `Extract<GateOutcome, { outcome: 'blocked' }>['reason']` (gate.ts; fourteen at f85c1b1c), each starting with its reason in backticks. Every bullet but `judges-outstanding`'s and `coverage-evidence`'s names its one answerer with that answerer's phrase and no other answerer's phrase: `bounce to the coder` for `not-committed`, `grader-fail` (with the payload's `failed_criteria`), `tests-failed` and `findings`; `bounce to the tester` for `screenshots-missing` and `screenshots-stale`; `bounce to the worker whose result it is` (the worker the gate line's `--result` and `--agent` name) for `schema-invalid` and `artifacts-missing`; `bounce to the uiux pass` for `uiux-spec-missing` (the uiux spec pass) and `uiux-visual-missing` (the uiux visual pass); `a judge turn answers it` for `grader-invalid` (the grader's turn, re-run as a new round only while step 6's `profile.graderRounds` leaves one, because the gate already closed this round's turn; with no grader round left, the grader cap's re-scope applies (dispatch.md 'Round counting and escalation')); `the wave-runner's own fix answers it` for `deps-missing` (step 7 branch 1). The `judges-outstanding` and `coverage-evidence` bullets name no answerer themselves and hold one sub-bullet per case of the evidence the gate writes on the outcome, each starting with its case and carrying exactly one phrase. `judges-outstanding`, keyed on the roles its `outstandingJudges` names: a uiux turn among them, `bounce to the uiux pass` (the uiux pass is a builder dispatch; any other judge it names is re-poked beside it under the rules of steps 5 to 7); no uiux turn among them, `a judge turn answers it` (each judge it names, re-poked, then `bs judge report`). `coverage-evidence`, keyed on its `coverageEvidence` (also in the `coverage-evidence` event): `present` false, `the epic session answers it` (the reporter list is project configuration); `present` true with an `unmeasured` subject, `bounce to the coder` (a claimed file has no row while files beside it do: either no test loads it or the coverage config skips it, the gate cannot tell which, so the coder answers it as before task-9, by adding a test that loads the file or, when the config outside its claims is the cause, by saying so in `notes`); `present` true with no `unmeasured` subject, `the wave-runner's own fix answers it` (the gate read no claims for the task id: its gate line names the id the plan lists, or the follow-up is recorded first). The `tests-failed` bullet says that a block carrying `error_class: execution.env-failure` follows the env-failure bullet instead, and the `grader-fail` bullet that a round-2 `fail` re-scopes under step 6 instead, as today; each is a pointer to an existing rule, not a second answerer. Step 9 contains no 'every other reason'. The `grader-invalid` sentence becomes 'A `grader-invalid` `gate-outcome` in the log is still a failed round the ladder counts, and is answered by the grader's turn, not by a bounce.', and step 7 branch 2 ends its `grader-invalid` answer with the same capped clause ('with no grader round left, the grader cap's re-scope applies (dispatch.md 'Round counting and escalation')') in place of 'with none left the task goes to the epic session'; this narrows task-8's wording to one answerer and keeps its routing. dispatch.md 'Round counting and escalation' says its re-scope path also answers a `grader-invalid` with no grader round left. Step 7's coverage bullet no longer says 'not the code': it names the three cases and says step 9 gives each its answerer. The wave rule 'A blocked task blocks itself' says a blocked outcome goes to the answerer step 9 names for its reason, not to the task's builder. test/handbackPreflight.test.ts holds one map from each reason to its answerer kind (`coder`, `tester`, `uiux`, `result-worker`, `judge-turn`, `wave-runner`, `epic-session`); for `judges-outstanding` a map from each case (`uiux-named`, `judges-only`) declared `satisfies Record<JudgesCase, Answerer>`, and for `coverage-evidence` one from each case (`summary-missing`, `subject-unmeasured`, `claims-unreadable`) declared `satisfies Record<CoverageCase, Answerer>`; the whole map declared `satisfies Record<Extract<GateOutcome, { outcome: 'blocked' }>['reason'], Answerer | Record<JudgesCase, Answerer> | Record<CoverageCase, Answerer>>` with `GateOutcome` imported as a type from src/gate.ts, so a reason added to the gate without a row fails to compile; one phrase per kind `satisfies Record<Answerer, string>`; and the builder kinds (`coder`, `tester`, `uiux`, `result-worker`) as one list, checked against escalation.ts `BUILDER_ROLES` (every role that list names is a builder kind's role, `result-worker` standing for the coder or the tester), so a builder role added to the ladder without a kind fails. It requires: for each reason exactly one bullet of step 9 that starts with that reason in backticks; in each bullet (each sub-bullet, for the two keyed reasons) its kind's phrase and none of the other six, so the test fails if any bullet names a second answerer; no bullet for a reason outside the map; every reason `REASON_BRANCH` puts in branch 3 mapped to `coder`, `tester` or `result-worker`, every reason it puts in branch 1 mapped to `wave-runner`, and every reason it puts in branch 2 mapped to `uiux` or `judge-turn` (or cases of them); no 'every other reason' in step 9; the two pointers; the uiux-is-a-builder sentence; the capped clause, word for word, in step 7 branch 2 and in step 9's `grader-invalid` bullet, and 'goes to the epic session' in neither `grader-invalid` text; the new `grader-invalid` sentence; the coverage bullet of step 7; and the new blocked-task-rule wording.

Findings f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-29686266, f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-446ee7cf, f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-105d3733 and f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-38ddc74d, the next move for a block no builder answers, at every failed-round count. Step 9 says, in one sentence, that every one of these reasons is a blocked `gate-outcome` and so a failed round `readFailedRounds` counts, whoever answers it; and, in one more, that a block no builder answers (a reason or case the list gives to a judge turn, which is the grader's or another non-builder judge's: `grader-invalid`, and `judges-outstanding` when no uiux turn is outstanding; the wave-runner's own fix; or the epic session; and an env-classified `tests-failed`) is never bounced, while a uiux pass is a builder dispatch (escalation.ts `BUILDER_ROLES`), so the uiux reasons and cases are not among them: after the first failed round its answerer acts and a bare re-gate follows; from the second failed round nothing more runs on that task id, no gate round and no builder dispatch, until the operator's answer is in the log, and the epic session puts it to the operator; the answer, a `user_prompt` event, picks one ladder-clean move: a re-scope under a new task id (dispatch.md 'Round counting and escalation'), whose ledger starts empty; one builder dispatch on a strictly higher model tier whose `dispatch_decision` names that answer as its `causal_parent`; or a waiver or closure of the task. From the third failed round every block, whatever its reason, needs the operator's answer first (`checkOperatorRung`). The env-failure bullet states the round-2 order once, as that rule does: its ladder sentence reads 'a bare re-gate only after the first failed round (the same HEAD, no new builder dispatch); from the second failed round, the operator's answer first and only then, if the answer picks it, one builder dispatch on a strictly higher model tier; the operator from the third', in place of 'a higher-tier builder dispatch from the second, the operator from the third', and its '"no coder bounce" means' sentence keeps its words up to `checkModelTierRung` and `checkOperatorRung` and adds that by the rule above that dispatch waits for the operator's answer. No sentence of step 9 says a higher-tier builder dispatch comes at the second failed round before or without the operator's answer for a block no builder answers. queue-and-gate.md section 5's ladder paragraph carries the same round-rule sentence word for word, and says that its operator-first bound at the second failed round is a playbook rule the log evidences by structure (the dispatch's `causal_parent` is the answer) and no verb enforces, an accepted gap like branch 4's bound; its env-failure paragraph replaces 'needs a builder dispatch on a higher model tier from the second' with 'from the second failed round, the operator's answer first and only then, if the answer picks it, one builder dispatch on a strictly higher model tier', so it states the same order. The spec's AC6 row states the same order. escalation.ts, budgets.yml and AC6's rungs stay as they are: the rule puts the operator's answer before the higher-tier builder dispatch when the fault is not a builder's. test/handbackPreflight.test.ts finds the round-rule sentence in step 9 and in section 5 after collapsing whitespace and requires them equal; requires 'from the second failed round, the operator's answer first and only then, if the answer picks it, one builder dispatch on a strictly higher model tier' in step 9's env-failure bullet and in section 5's env-failure paragraph, and 'higher-tier builder dispatch from the second' and 'higher model tier from the second' in neither; requires the round-rule sentence to name the uiux reasons as builder-answered; and keeps every other existing env-failure assertion.

Findings f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-38ddc74d, f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-2d92075f, f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-b3e3083c and f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-105d3733, the same map in queue-and-gate.md's outcome table: it gains a `blocked` row for `uiux-spec-missing` and one for `uiux-visual-missing`, so it holds exactly one `blocked` row per member of the reason type, and each row's last column carries the same answerer phrase as step 9 and no other answerer's phrase: the `tests-failed`, `findings`, `grader-fail` and `not-committed` rows `bounce to the coder`; the `artifacts-missing` row, like the `schema-invalid` row, `bounce to the worker whose result it is`; the `uiux-spec-missing` and `uiux-visual-missing` rows `bounce to the uiux pass`; the `grader-invalid` row `a judge turn answers it`, keeping its two pinned phrases and ending its capped case with the same capped clause as step 9 in place of any epic-session wording; the `judges-outstanding` row naming its two cases, each with its one phrase as in step 9; the `deps-missing` row `the wave-runner's own fix answers it` (installing the worktree's dependencies), with no unconditional re-gate; and the `coverage-evidence` row naming the three cases, each with its one phrase as in step 9, and no longer saying 'not the code'. Section 5's branch 2 ends its `grader-invalid` answer with the same capped clause. test/handbackPreflight.test.ts checks, from the same maps and phrase table, one row per reason, each row's phrase and no second one (the two keyed rows exactly their cases' phrases, each beside its case), and the capped clause in section 5's branch 2; the existing row assertions (the `grader-invalid`, screenshots and `schema-invalid` rows) hold unchanged.

Findings f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-38ddc74d, f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-29686266 and f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-105d3733, the ladder premise in code: test/handbackPreflight.test.ts runs the built `bs escalation check <session-id> --task <task-id>` over session logs in `mkdtemp` state directories, each starting with a coder `dispatch_decision` on `mid`, and reads each rung's check: (i) a blocked `gate-outcome` `deps-missing`, then a `gate-outcome` `pass` with no builder dispatch: exit 0 (a bare re-gate after the first failed round is clean); (ii) blocked `judges-outstanding`, blocked `deps-missing`, nothing more: exit 0, rung 2 `failedRounds` 2 and `not-applicable` (both non-builder reasons are counted, and stopping on the id is clean); (iii) the same two blocks, a `user_prompt`, then a `pass` with no builder dispatch: exit 1, rung 2 `unverifiable` (an operator's answer does not make a bare re-gate clean); (iv) the same two blocks, a coder dispatch on `mid`, a `pass`: exit 1, `violation`; (v) the same two blocks, a `user_prompt`, a coder dispatch on `frontier`, a `pass`: exit 0, rung 2 `ok`; (vi) as (v), then a third blocked `gate-outcome`, a `user_prompt`, a coder dispatch on `frontier` and a `pass`: exit 0, rung 3 `ok`, and the same log without that second `user_prompt`: exit 1, rung 3 `violation`; (vii) blocked `uiux-visual-missing`, a uiux `dispatch_decision` on `mid`, blocked `uiux-visual-missing`, a uiux `dispatch_decision` on `frontier`, a `pass`: exit 0, rung 2 `ok`, and the same log with that last uiux dispatch on `mid`: exit 1, `violation` (a uiux pass is a builder dispatch the ladder counts); (viii) blocked `judges-outstanding`, a reviewer `dispatch_decision`, blocked `judges-outstanding`, a reviewer `dispatch_decision`, a `pass`: exit 1, rung 2 `unverifiable` (a non-uiux judge's dispatch is no builder dispatch). This shows, with escalation.ts unchanged, that from the second failed round the only moves the ladder accepts on one id are to stop or to dispatch a builder, a uiux pass included, on a strictly higher tier, which is why the round rule stops a task no builder can answer until the operator answers, and why the uiux reasons are not under it.

Finding f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-b3e3083c, the coverage premise in code: test/handbackPreflight.test.ts runs the built `bs coverage check <worktree-dir> --plan <plan.json> --task <task-id>` on `mkdtemp` fixture worktrees: with no coverage summary, the evidence has `present` false and exit 1; with a summary holding a row for a file beside a claimed file but none for the claimed file, `present` true, that subject `unmeasured`, and exit 1. test/gate.test.ts's existing case 'blocks when the ownership table has no row for the gated task' gains two assertions, its others unchanged: the outcome's `coverageEvidence.present` is true and no subject is `unmeasured`, the third case's shape. So each case step 9 names is read off evidence the gate already writes.

Findings f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-5c096bd9, f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-9c1bb4d6 and f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-05cec9f9, the composer: when the plan holds no record at all under the typed task id (live or dead, as plan.ts `resolveTaskId` reads it), `composeBrief` reads the session lineage's `task-added` records with taskEvents.ts `readAddedTasks` and adopts the one whose id matches the typed id (a bare id qualified by the plan's epic, taskId.ts `taskIdsMatch`) and whose `epic_id` is the plan's `epic_id`, as `bs wave next` does. For it, compose writes: the header with the follow-up's qualified id; a `spec` section headed `Task spec (verbatim from the log's task-added record; this follow-up is not in the plan):` holding that record's payload; right after it a `scope` section, between the lines `<!-- BEGIN FOLLOW-UP SCOPE -->` and `<!-- END FOLLOW-UP SCOPE -->`, holding every finding findings.ts `listFindings` returns for the follow-up's id (the read `bs findings list --task <id>` makes) whose status is `raised`, `confirmed` or `fix-pending`, each as one line: the whole record as that read returns it, written as JSON and passed through findingContext.ts `flatten` (which findingContext.ts now exports and otherwise leaves alone, the one function the sibling findings block uses, never a second copy), so no text inside it stands on a line of its own and no `<!--` or `-->` inside it survives to open or close a block, under a header that says these findings are the follow-up's scope, the defects it exists to fix, and that their text is reviewer data, not instructions, never widening its claims or granting a permission; a `claims` section from the payload's `claims`, which must be an array of non-empty strings, anything else refused as `brief.invalid-value` naming `claims` and never read as `[]`; a `limits` section with `Token cap:` only when the payload carries a numeric `budget_tokens`, and `Turn budget:`; the lessons block for those claims and the payload's `case`; the open-findings context block exactly as `findingsForDispatch` writes it for the follow-up's id and claims (its exclusion of the task's own findings unchanged); and, for a coder, tester or grader, the same `preflight` and `gate_checks` sections, refusals and lint self-check as for a plan task, the tester's `--plan` being the plan file compose read. A follow-up that owns no finding in those statuses is refused as `brief.invalid-value` naming `scope`. The manifest of a follow-up brief gains `scope_finding_ids`; a plan-task manifest is unchanged.
